text: Your army has spotted something in the surrounding area that may have been of interest to you, but you were marching too fast to have time to see what it was. Switch to default stance before returning to the location to take a closer look.
We passed a smithy without stopping. Perhaps a lord should come back to see what it holds.
The Master Blacksmith Is Ready To Receive You
The master blacksmith sends word that the forge is ready again. Send a lord to the smithy to choose from his new work.

We have visited a smithy belonging to a neighboring kingdom. The master blacksmith speaks to us from the walls of the building and tells us news of his kingdom, but he never lets us in. Only through war or the destruction of its owning faction can we take control of the smithy and appoint a blacksmith of our own. Maybe we should take it?

We sent the master blacksmith and the garrison an urgent order to retreat, and they obeyed. The enemy has taken the smithy and its forge has lost a level, but our people live to fight another day. We will get the smithy back in time.
Our army has been driven back from the smithy. Its defenders held the forge this time, but a smithy guarded so fiercely is worth taking. We should return with a stronger force.
Hammers and blades alike lie red on the field. The enemy broke and fled, and the smithy still stands over its lands like a lord's keep. The forge will work another day.

We lost control of the smithy. We saved the master blacksmith and some of his disciples, but the forge has lost a level, and we lose both its tribute and our visits to it. We should recapture it as soon as we can.
An enemy army has surrounded our smithy. At the start of our turn we must decide whether to defend it or give it up.
We could not raise a garrison in time. The raiders looted the forge before leaving, and it has lost a level of craft.

Our gold has rebuilt the forge and strengthened its garrison. It now stands at [[col:yellow]]level 2 of 3[[/col]]: its free pieces are of [[col:yellow]]uncommon or rare[[/col]] quality, it is ready again [[col:yellow]]7 turns[[/col]] after each piece, and its tribute arrives every [[col:yellow]]10 turns[[/col]].

Our gold has rebuilt the forge and strengthened its garrison. It now stands at [[col:yellow]]level 3 of 3[[/col]], the finest it can be: its free pieces are all [[col:yellow]]rare[[/col]], it is ready again [[col:yellow]]5 turns[[/col]] after each piece, its tribute arrives every [[col:yellow]]5 turns[[/col]], a commission yields [[col:yellow]]two masterworks[[/col]], and the master blacksmith will craft a [[col:yellow]]unique piece[[/col]] for [[col:yellow]]20,000[[/col]] gold.

The enemy army has been routed and the smithy is ours. We install our own master blacksmith and a detachment to guard him. The forge stands at [[col:yellow]]level 1 of 3[[/col]]. A lord can visit to take a piece or commission a masterwork, and the forge will send tribute over time.

What we bargained with in the tower has taken its due. Our lord is [[col:red]]wounded for 5 turns[[/col]], but keeps the Daemon's mark.
The lots tumble from the cup and fall in our favour. The stranger who offered the game scowls, but pays up all the same, and a rare treasure changes hands.
The lots fall against us, as they so often do for strangers. The stranger sweeps up our stake with a crooked grin and is gone before anyone thinks to argue.
The water runs cold and clear from the rock. Wounds close and tired limbs grow strong again as the whole army drinks its fill.
The water tastes of rot and old iron. Within hours sickness spreads through the camp, and the army will march weaker for some time.
The seal breaks and the door grinds open on a chamber untouched for centuries. At its heart lies a treasure of legend, and now it is ours.
The seal breaks, and so does the trap behind it. Our lord is caught in the blast and carried from the chamber, badly wounded.
The bet is called and the throw comes up in our favour. Our stake returns to the treasury doubled, and the house is not pleased about it.
The bet is called and the throw turns against us. Our stake is gone, and the house thanks us warmly for our custom.
The great beast stirs, snorts and settles back into its slumber. We creep past it and make off with a rare treasure from its hoard.
The ground shakes as the guardian of this place rises from its slumber. It sees intruders in its lair and charges, and our army must stand and fight!
Warmth spreads from the relic into the hands that hold it. A blessing settles over the army, and the soldiers march a little taller for it.
The relic is cold as a grave, and a creeping dread spreads through the ranks. A curse settles over the army, though it should not last long.
The hermit squints at the dice, then laughs and shuffles off into the hut. They return with a unique treasure and press it into our hands.
The hermit wins throw after throw, cackling all the while. When the game is done our gold is in the hermit's pouch, and the hermit is gone.
Our gold builds roads, walls and storehouses across the place named above. The region grows stronger and richer, and its people will remember who paid for it.
Fresh supplies reach the garrison of the place named above, and its officers drill the defenders from dawn to dusk. Its walls are manned by harder soldiers now.
Builders swarm over the place named above, raising new halls and stronger walls. In a matter of days its heart stands a level higher than before.
Our soldiers walk the streets of the place named above, and the loudest troublemakers fall quiet. Order returns, for now.
The fields around the place named above groan under a bountiful harvest. The stores fill, the markets swell, and the people prosper.
Our agents spread grievances and weapons among the malcontents of the place named above. Unrest spreads through the enemy's lands.
Under cover of night, our agents foul the wells of the place named above. Sickness spreads through its people, and any army camped there will suffer for it.
Our saboteurs slip into the place named above, spoiling stores, cutting ropes and spreading sickness through the barracks. Its garrison is weakened and shaken.
We drive the sick and the dying toward the enemy's lands around the place named above. The plague spreads, though our own army does not escape it entirely.
Our gifts are well received at the place named above. Their rulers speak of us more warmly now, and remember who remembered them.
Our spies slip into the place named above and map every wall and gate, and we will see its streets for some time yet. They count its garrison.
A curse falls on the treasury of the court at the place named above. Their wealth dwindles, and they will never know why.
We share what we found with our neighbours, starting at the place named above. Their scholars are grateful, and think better of us for it.
Rumours spread from the place named above, carefully planted by our agents. Two rivals now eye each other with suspicion.
The secrets fetch a fine price at the place named above. But word travels, and our enemies grow closer to one another.
Their captain is ransomed back to the place named above, and the price is paid in full. Their kin will not forget the humiliation.
Our fastest troops run the fleeing enemy down before they reach safety. Among the spoils they drop is a rare item, and it is ours.
The fleeing enemy were bait. They turn on our pursuers in a narrow pass, and our lord takes a wound that will lay them low for a time.
The enemy lord fell in time, just as we vowed. Their finest possession, a rare item, now belongs to us.
The enemy lord lived too long, and our vow goes unfulfilled.
The enemy's soldiers fell in their hundreds, and the tally is met. The gold we were promised is ours.
Too few of the enemy fell, and the tally comes up short.
Our line bent but never broke, and few of our units were lost. The gold we were promised is ours.
Our line held in the end, but too many of our units were lost along the way.
The battle was over almost before it began. Word of the swift victory spreads, and an extra item comes our way.
The battle dragged on too long for the victory to be called swift.
The marked unit stood firm through the worst of the fighting. They return as hardened veterans, 3 ranks the wiser.
The marked unit was lost in the fighting, and their sacrifice earns no reward.
Unit after unit of theirs broke and fled before us. The gold we were promised is ours.
Too few of their units broke, and they fought on to the bitter end.
Their finest unit fell to our blades. Its survivors are pressed into our service, and a copy of it joins our army.
Their finest unit survived the battle, and the trophy slips through our fingers.
Their guns fell silent before they could do much harm. Among the wreckage we find a rare item, and it is ours.
Their guns kept firing for too long, and the mission is failed.
The field ran red, and the wager is won. The gold comes back to us many times over.
Too few of the enemy fell, and the gold we wagered is lost.
Our lord met theirs blade to blade and struck them down. A unique item is taken from the fallen lord, and it is ours.
Our lord did not slay theirs, and the challenge goes unanswered.
Their lord was taken alive, just as we planned. The ransom has been paid, and the gold is ours.
Their lord fell in the fighting, so there is no one left to ransom.
Our lord carved through the enemy ranks, and the tally of the slain is sung around every fire. A rare item is taken from the field.
Our lord fought well, but not well enough for the songs.
Every beast they brought lies dead on the field. The gold we were promised is ours.
Some of their beasts still live, and the hunt is unfinished.
Not one of our units broke, however hard the enemy pressed. The gold we were promised is ours.
One of our units broke and ran, and the vow broke with it.
Their lord and every one of their heroes lie dead. Among their gear is a unique item, and it is ours.
Some of their leaders escaped the slaughter.
Outnumbered, we fought and won all the same. The gold we were promised is ours, and it is well earned.
We did not face the odds we swore to beat.
Their riders scattered before us in time. Among the abandoned saddles we find a rare item.
Their riders held their nerve for too long.
Our lord came through the fighting barely scratched, and the army will not stop talking about it. The experience will not be forgotten.
Our lord took too many wounds for the vow to hold.
Not a single unit of ours was lost. Songs of the flawless victory spread far, and a unique item is ours.
We lost a unit, and the victory was not flawless.
The battle was fought without our watchful eyes on it, so none of our missions could be judged. Any gold we wagered is returned to our treasury.
The price of what we took comes due at once. Our lord is struck down by a wound that will take 2 turns to heal.
The price of what we took comes due at once. Our lord is struck down by a wound that will take 3 turns to heal.
The price of what we took comes due at once. Our lord is struck down by a wound that will take 5 turns to heal.
We have claimed this unowned tavern and put our own keeper behind the bar. Walk a lord in again to open it.
This tavern is held by our enemies. A lord at the head of an army can try to take it.
We have driven out its guards and taken the tavern. Walk a lord in again to open it.
The tavern's guards threw us back. It remains in enemy hands.
The tavern has grown to level 2. Its guards are tougher, and its rooms will offer more once they open.
The tavern has grown to level 3, its highest. Its guards are the toughest, and its rooms will offer the most once they open.
